rule: Founder, 26 November 2026: an AI may research, organize sources and draft, and never approves its own historical claims. A published museum record is existing source material that itself needs review; it is not human-approved. A claim is approved by a named human reviewer with the right expertise, then by the museum's editor for wording, uncertainty and tone. The founder approves the product and its scope and is never recorded as the historical authority. Until reviewers are named, no new historical claim is published as verified and every entry stands as 'historical review pending'.

kinds.sourced: text or a fact taken from, or linked to, a museum record: existing source material, not yet reviewed by a person
kinds.uncertain: a claim the source gives as approximate or disputed, or one the game derives from a source
kinds.reconstruction: something shown as it might have looked, with no reviewed source behind it
kinds.fiction: invented for play, and said to be on the page
kinds.convention: a way of counting or naming, not a claim

entries.claim: The game is set in the emirate of Granada under the Nasrids and is called 'The Last Kingdom of al-Andalus'; the founder's design sets it in 1475.
entries.context: Title, subtitle and the opening brief
entries.uncertainty: The title is the founder's. The year 1475 is the design's and is not stated by a museum record as a year of anything; it is a setting, not an event.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: The valley, its steward, its crops, prices and seasons are invented for play.
entries.context: The note on the opening brief ('This is a game, not a history')
entries.uncertainty: None: it is said to be invented.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: Eleven real places are named, each where the museum places it, and the distances between them are measured from the museum's coordinates.
entries.context: The rules' regional distances; the records linked from the brief
entries.uncertainty: The coordinates are of the places today; the distances are straight lines over the globe, not roads of the time.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: The brief links the museum's records of the Alhambra, the Generalife, the Nasrid palaces, the madrasa of Granada, the Nasrid entry into Granada, the building of the Alhambra, the fall of Granada, and Ibn al-Khatib's history of Granada.
entries.context: The opening brief, 'The setting, in the museum'
entries.uncertainty: The game states nothing about them itself: it shows each record's own label and links to it.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: Five ideas behind the game's mechanics are linked to museum records: market inspection, matching soil and water, improvements to the water-lifting wheel, tiraz textiles, lustreware.
entries.context: The records the game links to for the ideas behind its mechanics
entries.uncertainty: The link says the idea is real, not that the game models it faithfully. The game's numbers are invented.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: The look of the valley: lime-washed houses with clay-tile roofs, a mosque with a square minaret, a watermill with a wheel, a stone bridge of three arches, ox-carts, the dress of the people who walk.
entries.uncertainty: No museum record or reviewed source stands behind any of these shapes. They are the developer's general picture of a village of the western Mediterranean and are not stated anywhere as fact; under the founder's rule of 26 November 2026 they may not be presented as the architecture or dress of Nasrid Granada until a named reviewer has seen them.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent
entries.note: First for review when a reviewer is appointed.

entries.claim: Wheat stands ripe in late spring, olives grow on a terrace behind a broken channel, a meadow waits for water; the scenario runs ninety-six days, to the end of winter.
entries.uncertainty: Invented for play and covered by the note on the brief.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: The district is fictional; costs, yields and prices are game numbers, not historical figures.
entries.context: Help, and the note beside the museum links
entries.uncertainty: None: it is said to be fictional.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: Each chapter's brief quotes the museum's own account of the history behind it and links two records.
entries.context: The briefs of the three chapters
entries.uncertainty: The words quoted are the museum's summaries, unaltered; the game adds none of its own.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: Each tool and building is linked to the museum's record of the real thing behind it.
entries.context: The construction tools and their descriptions
entries.uncertainty: The link says the thing is real, not that the building in the game works as it did.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: Each research project is linked to a museum record.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: An endowment sets a sum aside for ever, and its yield pays a public building's upkeep: 'the game's form of the waqf'.
entries.uncertainty: The principle (the principal kept, the yield given) is the museum's record; the sums and the rule that a building then costs nothing are the game's.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: Droughts, silted canals and fevers that 'come with the caravans' strike the district.
entries.uncertainty: Invented events in a fictional district. Under the founder's rule they are to be shown with mitigation and recovery, not as spectacle: a hospital, a granary and a cleared canal are the game's answers.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: The look of the district: houses, domes, a bath, a library, a hospital, a water wheel.
entries.uncertainty: No museum record or reviewed source stands behind these shapes. They are generic and are not stated as the architecture of Abbasid Baghdad; they may not be presented as such until reviewed.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: Every round takes its name, its place, its coordinates and its year from one museum record: 2,125 rounds at 568 places in the pack.
sources: the museum records named in gaming/games/atlas/data/pack.v1.json, by id
entries.uncertainty: The game writes no statement of history of its own. Each record carries its own sources and its own uncertainty; a year or a place that is approximate in the record is approximate in the game, and the score allows for the record's precision.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: The region shown by the hint is the museum's own name for the region the place lies in.
sources: the museum's region names, as read by gaming/games/atlas/tools/build-pack.ts
entries.uncertainty: Regions are broad and modern in their naming; a region without a name in all seven languages is not offered.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: Centuries are counted as historians count them: 701 to 800 is the eighth.
entries.author: Claude Code (claude-fable-5-2), an AI agent

entries.claim: 263 events named for one place and scored at another are held out of the game.
entries.uncertainty: These are questions for the museum's data, not statements by the game: each is listed with the record to look at.
